workflows.name: Store Footprint Expansion Site Suitability & Strategic Assessment

Automation Opportunity: - GIS-based automatic trade-area analysis and demographic scorecards.
Controls: - CTL-764 (ensure controlled execution — Land Feasibility, Site Acquisition & Title Consolidation (PA-178.1).)
- CTL-764: Real Estate Committee formal approval required before title search; board authorization limits adhered to.
Cross-references: - links to VS-33 (strategy), VS-17.4 (FP&A), VS-112 (PMO), VS-57 (competitive intelligence)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Zoning misalignment**: Site fails locational clearance later; mitigated by early CLUP review in step 1.
System Touchpoints: - Strategy/FP&A (VS-33/VS-17.4), location master (VS-29), real estate GIS tool.

steps.a: Director, Facilities & Real Estate & Land Acquisition
steps.activity: Perform physical site evaluation: check plot area (8,000-15,000 sqm), frontage width, traffic access, utility availability, and terrain stability.
steps.r: Director, Facilities & Real Estate & Land Acquisition

steps.a: Director, Facilities & Real Estate & Land Acquisition
steps.activity: Conduct market mapping: analyze regional trade area, competitor density (VS-57), household income, and trade-pro concentration.
steps.r: Director, Facilities & Real Estate & Land Acquisition

steps.a: Director, Facilities & Real Estate & Land Acquisition
steps.activity: Prepare preliminary financial model: estimate acquisition cost, site-prep Capex, target payback period, and net present value (NPV).
steps.r: Director, Facilities & Real Estate & Land Acquisition

steps.a: Director, Facilities & Real Estate & Land Acquisition
steps.activity: Draft site suitability report and route to Real Estate Committee for stage-gate approval (VS-112).
steps.r: Director, Facilities & Real Estate & Land Acquisition

fields.Owner: Legal & Compliance Counsel / Land Acquisition Manager
fields.Participants: Legal Operations (VS-100), Registry of Deeds (RD) liaison, Geodetic Engineer

workflows.name: Land Ownership Search, Title Verification & Due Diligence

Automation Opportunity: - Title document OCR analysis for detecting standard encumbrance clauses.
Controls: - CTL-141 (ensure land title & acquisition due diligence.)
- CTL-764: Certified True Copies of TCT signed by RD Registrar; legal due diligence sign-off mandated before purchase offer.
Cross-references: - links to VS-100 (legal operations), VS-161 (third-party risk)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fake Title / Fraud**: Overlapping titles or fraudulent TCTs; mitigated by physical root search at Registry of Deeds and local assessor verification.
System Touchpoints: - Registry of Deeds database, Municipal/City Assessor database, Legal matter system (VS-100).

steps.a: Legal & Compliance Counsel / Land Acquisition Manager
steps.activity: Request Certified True Copies of Transfer Certificates of Title (TCT) from the Registry of Deeds.
steps.r: Legal & Compliance Counsel / Land Acquisition Manager

steps.a: Legal & Compliance Counsel / Land Acquisition Manager
steps.activity: Trace title history (root search) to identify potential overlapping claims, land patents, or free patents.
steps.r: Legal & Compliance Counsel / Land Acquisition Manager

steps.a: Legal & Compliance Counsel / Land Acquisition Manager
steps.activity: Verify liens, mortgages, encumbrances, and pending litigations (lis pendens) annotated on the title.
steps.r: Legal & Compliance Counsel / Land Acquisition Manager

steps.a: Legal & Compliance Counsel / Land Acquisition Manager
steps.activity: Confirm land ownership matching with tax declarations and secure Certified True Copy of Tax Declarations from City/Municipal Assessor.
steps.r: Legal & Compliance Counsel / Land Acquisition Manager

fields.Trigger: Title verification (W5130) showing tax declarations or tax liens

workflows.name: Real Property Tax (RPT) Arrears Investigation & Settlement

Automation Opportunity: - LGU electronic tax payment portals integration.
Controls: - CTL-141 (ensure land title & acquisition due diligence.)
- CTL-764: Tax Clearance Certificate secured from LGU Treasurer; payment matched to escrow deduction rules.
Cross-references: - links to VS-79 (tax management), VS-15 (P2P), VS-97 (real estate portfolio)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Undisclosed tax liability**: Unrecorded local assessments causing transfer delays; mitigated by securing formal Tax Clearance Certificate in step 4.
System Touchpoints: - Municipal Treasury billing system, Tax management module (VS-79), ERP accounts payable (VS-15).

steps.activity: Request Certified Statement of Real Property Tax Liabilities from the City or Municipal Treasurer's Office.
Verify historical arrears, penalties, and interest accrued on both land and improvements.
Draft tax settlement agreement: compute total taxes due, negotiate deduction of arrears from the final purchase price.
Pay taxes at the Treasurer's Office and secure a Tax Clearance Certificate.

fields.Participants: Heirs of the deceased owner, Legal Operations (VS-100), Notary Public
fields.Trigger: Title search (W5130) showing deceased owner on TCT

workflows.name: Extrajudicial Settlement (EJS) of Estate Negotiation & Heir Consent

Automation Opportunity: - None (requires physical verification and signature gathering).
Controls: - CTL-141 (ensure land title & acquisition due diligence.)
- CTL-764: EJS signed by 100% of heirs; publication affidavit verified by Legal; estate tax paid and BIR CAR (Certificate Authorizing Registration) secured.
Pain Points / Risks: - **Dissenting heir claim**: Omitted heir contesting the sale; mitigated by thorough EJS publication and securing notarized waivers from all heirs.
System Touchpoints: - Civil Registry records, newspaper publication tracking, Legal contract library (VS-100).

steps.activity: Identify and locate all legal heirs of the deceased registered owner; compile family tree and birth/death certificates.
Negotiate settlement terms: distribute proceeds or arrange buy-out of minor/dissenting heirs' shares.
Draft the Deed of Extrajudicial Settlement of Estate with Absolute Sale (EJS-with-Sale).
Publish EJS in a newspaper of general circulation for three consecutive weeks as legally required under Rules of Court.
File EJS and proof of publication with the BIR for estate tax clearance and local Registry of Deeds for transfer.

fields.Participants: Adjacent Landowners, LGU City/Municipal Engineer, Denr-LMS (Land Management Services)
fields.Trigger: Approved due diligence (W5130); boundary dispute or technical overlap suspected

workflows.name: Boundary Dispute, Land Survey & Technical Description Verification

Automation Opportunity: - Geospatial coordinate mapping and automatic overlap detection against cadastral GIS.
Controls: - CTL-141 (ensure land title & acquisition due diligence.)
- CTL-764: Survey report sealed and signed by licensed Geodetic Engineer; DENR approved plan secured; adjacent owner sign-offs notarized.
Pain Points / Risks: - **Encroachment/Overlap**: Adjacent structures built on property, delaying site development; mitigated by mandatory physical survey and monumenting prior to DOAS.
System Touchpoints: - DENR LMS database, GIS survey mapping tool, Document management system (VS-88).

steps.activity: Obtain Approved Subdivision Plan, cadastral maps, and technical descriptions from the DENR Land Management Bureau.
Conduct physical boundary survey (re-survey and monumenting) to verify actual lot coordinates and areas.
Compare physical survey data with TCT technical descriptions to identify overlaps, encroaching structures, or easements.
Obtain boundary alignment sign-offs (Barangay/LGU mediation or amicable boundary agreement) from adjacent landowners.

fields.Owner: Legal & Compliance Counsel / Land Acquisition Manager
fields.Participants: Seller, Escrow Agent (Bank), CFO, CEO, Legal (VS-100), Treasury (VS-18)

workflows.name: Deed of Absolute Sale (DOAS) Negotiation, Drafting & Execution

Controls: - CTL-764 (ensure controlled execution — Land Feasibility, Site Acquisition & Title Consolidation (PA-178.1).)
- CTL-764: Dual officer signatures (COO/CFO/CEO) per corporate table of authority; notary verification; escrow release tied to notarized DOAS.
Cross-references: - links to VS-15 (P2P), VS-18 (treasury), VS-100 (legal), VS-79 (tax)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Tax Valuation Dispute**: BIR assessing zonal value higher than contract price, delaying CAR; mitigated by pre-calculation of zonal value in step 1.
System Touchpoints: - ERP accounts payable (VS-15), treasury payment systems (VS-18), Legal contract database (VS-100).

steps.a: Legal & Compliance Counsel / Land Acquisition Manager

steps.r: Legal & Compliance Counsel / Land Acquisition Manager

steps.a: Legal & Compliance Counsel / Land Acquisition Manager

steps.r: Legal & Compliance Counsel / Land Acquisition Manager

steps.a: Legal & Compliance Counsel / Land Acquisition Manager

steps.r: Legal & Compliance Counsel / Land Acquisition Manager

fields.Participants: Registry of Deeds, LGU Assessor, BIR (VS-79), Treasury (VS-18)
fields.Trigger: Executed DOAS (W5134) and BIR CAR (Certificate Authorizing Registration) release

workflows.name: Registry of Deeds (RD) Title Transfer & Registration

Automation Opportunity: - Land registration tracking spreadsheet / ERP workflow tracking.
Controls: - CTL-141 (ensure land title & acquisition due diligence.)
- CTL-764: Original TCT kept in secure fireproof archive vault; scanned copy uploaded to ERP asset master (VS-35).
Cross-references: - links to VS-88 (document control), VS-35 (fixed assets), VS-79 (tax)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Document rejection**: RD flags errors in technical description or name mismatch; mitigated by strict checklist pre-audit prior to submission.
System Touchpoints: - Registry of Deeds tracking portal, LGU Assessor system, Land title vault (VS-88).

steps.activity: Pay local Transfer Tax at the City/Provincial Treasurer's Office and obtain a Transfer Tax Receipt.
Submit complete transfer packet to the Registry of Deeds: old TCT, DOAS, BIR CAR, Tax Clearance, Transfer Tax Receipt.
Follow up on RD registration, pay registration fees, and obtain the new Transfer Certificate of Title (TCT) in BuildRight's name.
Apply for a new Tax Declaration under BuildRight's name at the City/Municipal Assessor's Office.

fields.Frequency: A recurring Philippine landbanking hazard: expect a handful of new occupation events per year across the banked portfolio, clustered where banked lots adjoin urbanizing barangays — rising with every year a parcel is held pre-development
fields.Participants: Director, Facilities & Real Estate (portfolio decisions), Legal Counsel (VS-100 ejectment and title actions), Geodetic Engineer (the W5133 survey class), the caretaker network, Barangay & LGU officials (relocation and social welfare), PNP (syndicate and fake-deed cases), Corporate Security (VS-159 site-hardening and intelligence), Tax Accountant (W5131 RPT continuity)
fields.Trigger: Detection of new informal-settler structures, illegal occupants, or third-party possession claims on a banked (pre-development) BuildRight landholding — caretaker report, geotagged patrol or drone imagery, real-property-tax inspection, barangay/LGU notice, or a buyer/lessee appearing with documents executed by a fake attorney-in-fact
fields.Volume: 1 event × the occupied parcel (banked lots held 3–10 years ahead of the 10–15 store openings/year pipeline) × the occupant group (a few families to syndicate-scale settlements) × the resolution surface (barangay, LGU relocation track, courts, and where agrarian-adjacent, the DAR machinery)

workflows.name: Informal-Settler Invasion & Illegal Occupation of Banked Land — Detection, Relocation & Ejection Protocol

Automation Opportunity: - Drone-imagery change detection on banked lots with new-structure alerts (replaces manual patrol discovery)
- Occupation-log template with enforced geotagging and date-stamping (hardens Step 1's evidence chain)
- Inspection-cadence scheduler on the portfolio register with risk-tiered frequencies (replaces the manual Step 7 calendar)
- RPT renewal calendar tied to the land register (links to W5131) with escalation on arrears
Background: 'Informal settler'/'squatter'/'illegal occupation'/'adverse possession' appear in zero PA files. W5133 owns titled-neighbor boundary disputes, W5143 the agrarian tenant-compensation program, W5150 fencing only at groundbreaking, and construction-site security lives in VS-20's active build sites — but banked land sits vacant for years: occupation grows quietly, the acquisitive-prescription clock runs on possession that is uninterrupted, adverse, and under a claim of ownership (Civil Code prescription — documented assertions, police/LGU reports, and timely legal action interrupt continuity), professional-squatter syndicates under RA 7279 sell fake rights to innocents, and caretakers themselves can turn (spurious deeds, illicit leasing). Nobody owned the detect–document–negotiate–eject lifecycle, and the no-self-help rule — demolition or blocking entry without legal process creates criminal and administrative exposure and converts a property dispute into a human-rights complaint — had no guardian.
Controls: - CTL-141 (ensure land title & acquisition due diligence)
- CTL-764 (ensure controlled execution — Land Feasibility, Site Acquisition & Title Consolidation (PA-178.1).)
- operational: no eviction action without counsel sign-off; occupation evidence captured within 72 hours of detection; caretaker re-vetting annually; RPT continuity maintained on all banked parcels
Pain Points / Risks: - **Prescription-ripening risk**: years of unchallenged possession mature into adverse-possession assertions against the title; mitigated by Step 1's 72-hour documentation and Step 5's timely filings that interrupt continuity
- **Self-help backlash**: a landlord-style demolition or blockade creates criminal exposure, LGU complaints, and viral incidents; mitigated by Step 3's legal-process-only rule with counsel sign-off

- **Innocent-purchaser tangle**: families who bought fake rights from syndicates complicate ejectment and attract political attention; mitigated by Step 2's classification and Step 4's relocation assessment before filing
- **Caretaker collusion**: the guard becomes the lessor or dealer; mitigated by Step 6's re-vetting and rotation plus Step 3's audit trail on documents executed over the parcel
- **Tax-lapse evidence risk**: RPT arrears on a banked parcel weaken possession assertions and invite LGU complications; mitigated by Step 7's RPT-continuity requirement
Staffing Implication: - Absorbed by the Landbanking team with Legal and Corporate Security support; no incremental headcount.
System Touchpoints: - Land-portfolio register with an occupation-status field, inspection cadence, and evidence attachments
- Geotagged photo/evidence repository (the W471-class evidence chain)
- Geodetic survey and technical-description records (links to W5133)
- RPT declaration and payment records (links to W5131 and the PA-97.3 property-tax chain)
- Legal case management (links to VS-100); caretaker contracts and vetting records (the VS-167 screening class)
Time Estimate: Detection and documentation ≈ 6–12 staff-hours per event; negotiated relocations run 1–6 months at 10–20 staff-hours of company effort; court-led ejections 6–24 months at 20–40 staff-hours. At the handful-of-events/year cadence ≈ 60–160 staff-hours/year across the portfolio, absorbed by the landbanking team and counsel.

steps.activity: **Evidence-first documentation within 72 hours**: geotagged photos, structure census, occupant headcount, drone imagery where flown, and a dated occupation log opened — the foundation of every later legal action and the prescription-interruption record

**Classification & strategy call**: genuine informal settlers (negotiation-led) vs professional-squatter syndicates (law-enforcement-led, RA 7279) vs the caretaker-fraud variant (internal investigation with VS-159/VS-100; fake-deed cases prosecuted); strategy recorded with rationale

**No-self-help discipline**: no fencing-people-out, demolition, or blocking of entry except through counsel-directed legal process; interim measures (signage, boundary marking) only with Legal sign-off — always

**Barangay & LGU engagement**: barangay certification of the occupation; the LGU relocation and social-welfare track (UDHA's relocation duty for qualified beneficiaries); negotiated relocation assistance assessed against the litigation alternative — the assessment documented either way

**Legal action**: Rule 70 ejectment (forcible entry within one year of entry; unlawful detainer thereafter) via VS-100; injunction against syndicate leaders; criminal complaints for estafa/falsification where fake documents surface
**Site protection**: perimeter fencing to the W5150 standard, signage, caretaker re-vetting and rotation, geotagged patrol cadence tiered to the occupation risk; gate and access control

**Portfolio watch**: every banked lot risk-tiered and inspected on cadence; RPT declarations kept current per W5131 (tax continuity as possession and title hygiene); title monitoring refresh per W5130

**Records & intelligence**: occupation log, resolution cost-and-duration register, and the syndicate modus file to VS-159; a development-schedule flag where occupation risk argues accelerating handover (the W5152 chain)
